sections.title: LUCID: Statistically Grounded Self-Correction for LLM Reasoning Evaluation
sections.abstract: LUCID combines prompt-based self-correction with design-based supervised learning to calibrate LLM ratings of reasoning steps, reporting improved calibration and downstream selection on several reasoning domains.
sections.claimed_contribution: The paper introduces LUCID and Design-based Supervised Learning (DSL); its abstract reports that LUCID narrows GPT-5-mini's calibration gap on PRM800K from 7.8 to 0.9 percentage points in one pass.
sections.unique_caveat: The authors state that prompt feedback shifts rating thresholds without improving class-balanced sound/unsound discrimination, leaving residual false alarms; supervised fine-tuning can outperform it when open weights are available and discrimination is the priority.
sections.ranking_evidence: Collector score 2.579; Hugging Face Papers featured 2026-11-24 with 1 upvote and 2 comments; 2 cross-list categories. Only candidate with recorded direct-attention signal in the supplied candidate list.

sections.title: ASTERISM: Do Multimodal LLMs Actually Look at All the Images?
sections.abstract: An audit of 19 multi-image benchmarks finds many items solvable from one image, and ASTERISM filters these shortcuts while proposing cross-image credit assignment for multimodal model training.
sections.claimed_contribution: The paper presents ASTERISM, an 18.7K-item audited multi-image benchmark, and cross-image credit assignment (CICA); the authors report 2.6–6.0 point gains over the base models on three open-source MLLMs.
sections.unique_caveat: The authors say the benchmark's domains and task mix inherit the 19 source datasets; CICA's main comparison uses three backbones, with larger multimodal models left for future work.
sections.ranking_evidence: Collector score 0.75 entirely from 3 cross-list categories; no paper-specific Hugging Face or Hacker News attention signal was recorded.

sections.title: Exploring Multi-Player Social Games as Verifiable Training Grounds for Large Language Models
sections.abstract: The paper studies supervised fine-tuning and reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards on three social games, reporting stronger Qwen3 play on trained games and transfer to three held-out games.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors use rule-decided social-game outcomes as a training reward; their abstract reports Qwen3-4B's win rate rising from 33% to 81% on trained games and from 39% to 54% on three held-out games against Gemma-3-27B.
sections.unique_caveat: The authors limit training to three hidden-role games, one opponent, and the Qwen3 family; they also report no human evaluation and note that transfer varies across game types and opponents.
sections.ranking_evidence: Collector score 0.75 from 3 cross-list categories, including cs.AI, cs.LG, and cs.MA; no paper-specific Hugging Face or Hacker News attention was recorded.

sections.title: Learning Compact State Abstractions for LLM Agents
sections.abstract: The authors search for inspectable recursive programs that compress interaction histories while preserving an agent's task performance, reporting substantially shorter inputs on ALFWorld and ScienceWorld.
sections.claimed_contribution: The paper defines state sufficiency by task performance and uses an LLM-guided genetic algorithm to discover deterministic recursive state programs; its abstract reports input reductions of up to 71% on ALFWorld and 57% on ScienceWorld while preserving near-reference success.
sections.unique_caveat: The abstract's reported evidence is confined to ALFWorld and ScienceWorld, so performance and robustness in other tasks or deployment settings remain unestablished here.
sections.ranking_evidence: Collector score 0.75 from 3 cross-list categories, including cs.AI, cs.CL, and cs.NE; no paper-specific direct-attention signal was recorded.

sections.title: GoldiBench: Right Tools, Wrong Amount -- Benchmarking Agents on Effect Judgement in Professional Editing
sections.abstract: GoldiBench tests whether agents can infer the right magnitude of edits from visual goals across five professional applications, finding a sharp gap between executing known settings and choosing settings from the desired effect.
sections.claimed_contribution: The paper introduces 500 target-rendered editing tasks across darktable, RawTherapee, GIMP, Inkscape, and Blender; its abstract reports that the best model passes 19% of program-based tasks when given tools but not their magnitudes.
sections.unique_caveat: The measured scope is 500 tasks in five applications, and the reported results do not establish whether the same effect-judgment gap holds across other tools or real-world workflows.
sections.ranking_evidence: Collector score 0.75 from 3 cross-list categories, including cs.AI and cs.CL; no paper-specific Hugging Face or Hacker News attention was recorded.
